The Popen with `start_new_session=True` calls setsid which... hmm, actually the failure occurs in the parent's `_execute_child` reading the error from the child — EPERM. The child's preexec_fn `child_setup` calls limits() then prctl(22, 2, filter) (seccomp). If seccomp load fails with EPERM, the child exits with that error which propagates as PermissionError from Popen. So it's likely the SECCOMP_SET_MODE_FILTER (prctl 22) not permitted in this dev container (needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN or a permissive no_new_privs setting) — or clone denied.

This is an environment limitation ("Ordinary non-root public execution needs Linux prctl subreaper/seccomp support"). Our dev container may lack seccomp permission. Let me verify by testing prctl(22,...) directly.

Either way, I can still test the pipeline using run.py directly (as I did). Let me check quickly whether it's seccomp.
